design_summary.choice: (a) -- gate the route on ACTOR_ACTIVE like its siblings. Rejected (b) whitelist: provides_coverage+holder_count answers the exact per-(role_id,employee_id) membership question rights-overview.ts's self-scope projection deliberately hides from an ordinary ACTIVE non-admin employee (that hiding is the whole reason T-0745 needed a new route in the first place); a deactivated caller -- no longer a legitimate party to the self-absence/substitute flow this route exists to serve -- must not get a strictly WIDER answer than a legitimate active non-admin already can't get through the normal channel. Whitelisting would require proving the boolean+count is harmless, which is impossible once that framing is accepted (real enumeration vector: pair a tenant-open GET /api/org roster with a per-substitute_employee_id probe over a known role_id).
design_summary.mechanism: resolveActiveActorEmployeeId (rights-intents.ts) -- an INDEPENDENT copy of registerSelfAbsence's own inline `slug = $2 AND ${ACTOR_ACTIVE_SQL}` actor-resolve, not a shared-helper refactor (extracting the code out of registerSelfAbsence's body would have made that already-registered T-0662 resolver's own text stop carrying the predicate literally, breaking FF-0662-1 for a resolver this task didn't need to touch). Called BEFORE the holder-set read; deactivated caller resolves to null -> 404 NOT_FOUND "actor employee record not found", byte-identical error shape to registerSelfAbsence's own denial (sibling-policy consistency, as the task requested).
design_summary.sibling_check: registerSubstitute/registerFire/registerHire/registerUrgentRevoke all route through loadAdminContext (admin gate, ACTOR_ACTIVE-carrying). registerSelfAbsence is the ONLY authority-writing sibling WITHOUT an admin gate (self-service, by design) -- and it carries its OWN bespoke ACTOR_ACTIVE check for exactly that reason. T-0745's read copied registerSelfAbsence's "no admin gate" half (correctly, for self-service parity) but not its "still ACTOR_ACTIVE-gate the caller" half -- this task closes that gap.

First draft of the new unit-test stub pool matched the coverage route's holder-set query with `!text.includes("employee_id")`, which excluded the query's OWN `SELECT employee_id FROM ...` text and broke the positive-control tests (c1/c2) with false-empty holder sets. Fixed by narrowing the exclusion to the actual FILTER shapes (`employee_id <>` / `employee_id = $3`) that distinguish this route's holder-set query from the substitute/self-absence sibling routes' tier-probe queries -- caught immediately by running the new test file before wiring it into the targeted suite.
